title: Latency & SLA Handoff Cheatsheet (Iter0)
content:
Purpose: quick reference slide-deck for Sales -> Solutions -> SRE handoffs on latency and SLA topics. This is intentionally concise: bullet-first, test scripts, demo checklist, and objection snippets.

Status: working draft. Use this when nudging prospects from 'we need faster' to concrete next steps (POC specs, service level targets, data required).

Slide 1 — TL;DR for AE (30s script)
- Opening: “We help you make LLM features predictable in latency and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.”
- Quick ask: “What p95 and tail latency do you need under expected concurrency? If you can share a 2-minute sample trace or synthetic workload, we can propose config (batching, quantization, routing).”
- Call to action: run live latency test during SE call; capture token counts and concurrency.

Slide 2 — Target metrics cheatsheet (reference numbers for field)
- Small convo (<=512 tokens): targeted p95 (hosted) 50–120ms, median 20–60ms.
- Long context (2k–8k tokens): p95 200–800ms depending on model and batch.
- Embeddings (per 768-d vector): 5–40ms p95.
- Sizing cue: if prospect expects sub-100ms p95 at >30 qps, recommend Dedicated or Private with pinned capacity.
- Note: numbers vary by model and quantization; always capture model name + seq length.

Slide 3 — Quick data we need from customer (one-pagers help)
- Sample prompt set: 20–50 representative requests (include typical token lengths).
- Expected concurrency and burst patterns (qps sustained vs burst).
- Target percentiles (p50, p95, p99) and whether tail for user-perceived latency or background batch ok.
- Security/placement requirements: public cloud, VPC-only, on-prem.
- SLA expectations (uptime, recovery RTO/RPO).

Slide 4 — Handoff checklist (sales -> SE -> infra)
- Sales collects: product use-case, business impact metric (engagement lift / throughput), cost sensitivity.
- SE: run synthetic replay against hosted with sample requests; capture response times, token counts, and cost estimate.
- SE: if p95 target unmet, attempt config changes: reduce batch size, enable prefix caching, try lower-precision quantized model variant. Document results.
- Infra/SRE: if moving to Dedicated/Private, validate network egress, KMS/K8s sizing, and disk IO for KV cache.
- Always: create a Triaged ticket in JIRA linking the test artifacts and a recommended next step (POC/pilot/Dedicated estimate).

Slide 5 — Demo play (30–45 min SE call)
- Prep: SE runs local synthetic against hosted model and records baseline. Have token counting widget ready.
- Live steps: 1) run baseline with sample prompt (shared screen), 2) ramp concurrency (locally simulated), 3) flip on batching/caching and show delta, 4) show cost delta in Console per 1M tokens.
- Talking points: explain tradeoffs (latency vs token economics) and tie to customer KPIs (latency -> conversion rates or agent throughput).

Slide 6 — Objections + rebuttals (latency-focused)
- Objection: "Our users need <50ms always". Rebuttal: "We can aim for sub-50ms median on certain models and context lengths, but for strict p95 under variable load we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity and traffic shaping; let's run a focused POC to quantify." 
- Objection: "Cloud cold-starts kill us." Rebuttal: "We have warm-pool strategies and autoscaling hooks; Dedicated avoids cold-starts by reserving capacity and Canary routing avoids noisy neighbors." 
- Objection: "Quantization will break quality." Rebuttal: "Use our Optimize toolkit to compare quantized candidates on your eval set; we typically see small deltas for classification/assistant tasks and big cost wins." 

Slide 7 — Quick config recipes (SE quick wins)
- If tail latency is bad and cost tolerance exists: reduce batch window size, increase concurrency threads, pin model to Dedicated.
- If cost is dominant and latency target lenient: enable aggressive batching and quantized variant (e.g., 4-bit) + prefix cache.
- For mixed workloads: route infrequent heavy contexts to dedicated pool and common short requests to hosted (smart routing policy).

Slide 8 — Competitor conversation snippets (concise)
- If they say "other vendor guarantees 99% <100ms": ask about token sizes, concurrency, and what model variants are used. Many public claims omit real tail behavior.
- If they push simpler managed endpoints: emphasize Redwood's routing, prefix caching, and Optimize toolkit for production cost control.

Slide 9 — Pricing cues to use in field (do not quote exact numbers)
- Use ranges: hosted per-token cost for gen vs embeddings; Dedicated has base commitment + usage; Private is platform licensing + infra.
- For initial sizing, present modeled 3-month cost under low/medium/high traffic scenarios. Attach sample spreadsheet.

Slide 10 — POC checklist (what to deliver to customer)
- Baseline latency report (p50/p95/p99), sample prompts, captured token counts.
- Config matrix tried (batch window, quant levels, model variants, routing).
- Cost delta table (tokens vs compute estimate) and recommended deployment mode.
- Security checklist for Private: KMS, VPC peering, audit log retention.

Slide 11 — FAQ / notes to SE
- Note: Always save raw traces (timestamps + token counts) — this speeds root cause.
- For very long contexts, KV cache hit rate is crucial; ask about typical prefix reuse.
- If customer says "we already use CPU-optimized open models", ask for model family and quantization status — we can often beat CPU cost with GPU batching for high throughput.

Appendix — TODOs and open questions (team action items)
- Verify current hosted p95 numbers for Mistral-7B v1 on us-west for 512-token median (Infra/Bench team).
- Create a short token-counting widget snippet for AE to send to customers (DevEx).
- Draft a one-page POC pricing template for AE use (Finance + GTM).
- Finalize a short recording script for SE demo that includes steps and expected numbers.

Endnotes: this deck is intentionally minimal so AEs and SEs can riff. Use linked Confluence doc for deep dives. Feedback welcome — add comments or ping @Jonah on Slack.

---
Internal history: spawned from field feedback Q4 2025 — multiple accounts asking for faster handoffs when latency targets were vague. This is iteration 0; will iterate after 3 trial handoffs.
